original_record.question: A rectangular piece of paper $F G H I$ with sides of length $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $16 \mathrm{~cm}$ is folded along the line $M N$ so that the vertex $G$ coincides with the vertex $I$ as shown. The outline of the paper now makes a pentagon $F M N H^{\prime} I$. What is the area, in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$, of the pentagon $F M N H^{\prime} I$ ? <image1>
original_record.solution: Since $M I=M G$, we have $F M+M I=16$, so $M I=16-F M$. By Pythagoras, $F M^{2}+F I^{2}=M I^{2}$ so $F M^{2}+16=(16-F M)^{2}$. So $F M^{2}+16=256-32 F M+F M^{2}$ so $32 F M=240$ and hence $F M=7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$. The same argument applies to triangle $H^{\prime} N I$ giving $H^{\prime} N=7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $I N=8.5 \mathrm{~cm}$.  The areas of triangles $H^{\prime} N I$ and $F M I$ are both $\frac{1}{2} \times 7.5 \times 4=15 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. The area of triangle $M N I=\frac{1}{2} \times 8.5 \times 4=17 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$, so the area of the pentagon is $15+15+17=47 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$.
